precision-references.title: Choose a shunt resistor
precision-references.prompt: A 2.048 V shunt needs 150 μA, the load needs 80 μA, and supply ranges from 2.7 to 3.3 V. Find the maximum feed resistance and the high-supply no-load reference current for 2.7 kΩ.
precision-references.hint: Use minimum supply for the current guarantee; maximum supply with no load for stress.

solution.step: Worst case for the current guarantee
solution.text: At minimum supply and full load, the resistor must still deliver the shunt's 150 µA plus the load's 80 µA.
Maximum supply, no load: everything flows into the shunt.
Confirm 464 µA is within the shunt's maximum current, and include resistor and reference tolerance.

solution.answer: $R$ ≤ 2.835 kΩ; with 2.7 kΩ the shunt carries up to 464 µA.

precision-references.title: Reference drift in codes
precision-references.prompt: A 12-bit ADC uses 2.5 V. The reference changes by +60 ppm while a fixed input is at 75% of nominal span. Estimate the code change.
precision-references.hint: Reference error scales the code with the opposite sign.

solution.text: The code is proportional to $V_{in}/V_{ref}$, so a +60 ppm reference lowers the code by 60 ppm.

solution.answer: About −0.18 code (112.5 µV); whether the output code flips depends on where the input sits within its bin.

precision-references.title: Size a first-pass reservoir
precision-references.prompt: A reference charge impulse is 80 pC. What ideal capacitance limits its immediate droop to 20 μV? Why is this not a complete design?
precision-references.hint: Use charge conservation before adding the drive impedance.

solution.text: Effective capacitance under DC bias, ESR and ESL, recovery before the next conversion, and buffer stability with that load.

solution.answer: At least 4 µF of effective capacitance, which is only a first pass.

precision-noise-grounding.title: Integrate a real low-pass
precision-noise-grounding.prompt: A flat 8 nV/√Hz density passes through a unity first-order 200 Hz low-pass. Find rms noise.
precision-noise-grounding.hint: Its noise bandwidth is larger than its −3 dB bandwidth.

precision-noise-grounding.title: A fast shared inductance
precision-noise-grounding.prompt: A 20 nH common return carries a current that rises by 0.25 A in 25 ns. Find the induced voltage.
precision-noise-grounding.hint: Use di/dt, not switching repetition frequency.

solution.answer: 0.2 V during the edge, wherever that return is shared.

precision-noise-grounding.title: Leakage in a current measurement
precision-noise-grounding.prompt: A 1 TΩ path from 3 V to a virtual-ground input feeds a 10 GΩ feedback resistor. Calculate output error; repeat with a guard at 3 mV.
precision-noise-grounding.hint: The guard changes voltage across the unwanted insulation.

solution.text: The leakage flows into the virtual ground and through the feedback resistor.
Now only 3 mV appears across the insulation.

solution.answer: 30 mV unguarded; 30 µV with the guard.

precision-calibration.title: Invert a measured line
precision-calibration.prompt: At 0.1 V a meter reads 2100 counts; at 2.1 V it reads 42100 counts. What corrected voltage corresponds to 17100 counts?
precision-calibration.hint: Fit slope and intercept, then invert.

precision-calibration.title: Choose excitation current
precision-calibration.prompt: A 1000 Ω sensor must dissipate no more than 0.05 mW. What current limit follows?
precision-calibration.hint: Power depends on the square of current.

precision-calibration.title: Separate sensor and thermal EMF
precision-calibration.prompt: A resistor measured at ±0.5 mA gives +50.007 mV and −49.993 mV. Find resistance and additive EMF.
precision-calibration.hint: Difference isolates the odd component; sum isolates the even component.

solution.answer: 100.000 Ω and 7 µV of thermal EMF.

power-linear-regulators.title: Can a current-rated LDO survive?
power-linear-regulators.prompt: A 9-to-3.3 V LDO delivers 0.3 A at 45 °C ambient. Assume 50 K/W and ignore quiescent loss. Estimate junction temperature.
power-linear-regulators.hint: Use the voltage difference, not output power, for pass loss.

solution.answer: About 130 °C, which is likely beyond the guaranteed range even though 0.3 A is within the current rating.

power-linear-regulators.title: Bound a load-step capacitor
power-linear-regulators.prompt: A 0.2 A increase must cause less than 40 mV droop before a 5 μs response. Ignore ESR first. What effective capacitance is required?

solution.answer: At least 25 µF effective; add margin for ESR, tolerance and DC-bias derating.

power-linear-regulators.title: Separate rejection from generated noise
power-linear-regulators.prompt: A 50 mV rms ripple lies at a frequency where PSRR is 40 dB. The LDO generates 300 μV rms independent noise in the measured band. Find combined rms.
power-linear-regulators.hint: Attenuate the ripple, then sum independent powers.

solution.text: 40 dB is a factor of 100.

power-buck-converters.title: Choose the inductor
power-buck-converters.prompt: Design an ideal 24-to-6 V buck at 400 kHz for 0.4 A peak-to-peak ripple. Find L and the CCM boundary.
power-buck-converters.hint: First derive duty, then use the rising ramp.

solution.text: The valley reaches zero when the average current equals half the ripple.

power-buck-converters.title: Find the capacitor stress
power-buck-converters.prompt: A buck supplies 2 A at duty 0.3 with small inductor ripple. What are average input current and input-capacitor rms current?
power-buck-converters.hint: Average source current and pulsed capacitor current are different.

solution.text: The capacitor supplies $I_{out}-I_{in}$ during the on-time and absorbs $I_{in}$ during the off-time.

solution.answer: 0.6 A average; 0.92 A rms in the input capacitor.

power-buck-converters.title: Test a low-load waveform
power-buck-converters.prompt: A diode buck has 0.6 A ripple and supplies 0.1 A. Is a waveform with −0.2 A valley physical?
power-buck-converters.hint: Check what can conduct reverse current.

solution.text: A diode cannot conduct backwards.
The inductor current stops at zero, giving discontinuous conduction. A forced-continuous synchronous converter could go negative, but that is a different mode.

solution.answer: No: a diode buck enters DCM instead.

power-boost-isolated.title: A boost current rating
power-boost-isolated.prompt: A 3-to-9 V ideal boost supplies 0.3 A with 0.4 A ripple. Find duty, average inductor current and peak.
power-boost-isolated.hint: Only the off interval supplies the output.

solution.text: The inductor feeds the output only during the off-time.

power-boost-isolated.title: Find negative-rail stress
power-boost-isolated.prompt: An ideal inverting buck–boost makes −12 V from +5 V. Find duty and approximate switch blocking voltage.
power-boost-isolated.hint: The inductor transfers to the output in a separate interval.

solution.text: When off, the switch sees the input plus the magnitude of the output.
Add overshoot and derating, and check the controller's pin references.

power-boost-isolated.title: A DCM flyback power estimate
power-boost-isolated.prompt: A flyback has 80 μH magnetizing inductance, 0.8 A peak current and 100 kHz switching. Estimate ideal power and output at 85% efficiency.
power-boost-isolated.hint: Each fully demagnetized cycle transfers one stored-energy packet.

power-control-layout.title: Test a sampled current loop
power-control-layout.prompt: An ideal peak-current loop has m₁ = 0.1 A/μs and m₂ = 0.3 A/μs. Find the minimum compensation slope for stability and the multiplier at mₐ = 0.2 A/μs.

solution.answer: Need $m_a$ > 0.1 A/µs; at 0.2 A/µs, λ = −1/3 (errors alternate and shrink).

power-control-layout.title: A capacitor eats the current budget
power-control-layout.prompt: A 470 μF output ramps to 3.3 V in 3 ms. The normal load draws 0.2 A. Estimate required current during the linear ramp.
power-control-layout.hint: Add capacitor current and load current.

power-control-layout.title: Locate a ringing frequency
power-control-layout.prompt: A switching loop has 20 nH and 500 pF equivalent capacitance. Estimate resonance and characteristic impedance.

solution.text: $Z_0$ sets the scale of a damping resistor; the snubber capacitor must be several times the 500 pF.

rf-impedance-matching.title: Translate a measured sine
rf-impedance-matching.prompt: A 0.4 V peak sine drives 50 Ω. Find power and dBm.

rf-impedance-matching.title: Design a resistance transformation
rf-impedance-matching.prompt: Match a 25 Ω source to 100 Ω at 1 MHz using series L and shunt C on the load.
rf-impedance-matching.hint: Derive Q, then series and shunt reactances.

solution.text: The shunt C goes across the larger (100 Ω) resistance; the series L goes on the 25 Ω side.
100 Ω in parallel with −j57.7 Ω equals 25 − j43.3 Ω; the series +j43.3 Ω cancels the reactance, leaving 25 Ω.

solution.answer: L = 6.89 µH in series, C = 2.76 nF across the 100 Ω load.

rf-impedance-matching.title: Interpret a return-loss claim
rf-impedance-matching.prompt: A port has 20 dB return loss at one frequency. Find reflection magnitude and reflected power fraction.
rf-impedance-matching.hint: Use amplitude dB for Γ, then square it.

solution.text: This describes the match at one frequency, not loss or bandwidth.

rf-signal-chains.title: Estimate a receiver floor
rf-signal-chains.prompt: At 290 K, a receiver has 3 dB NF, 20 kHz noise bandwidth and needs 12 dB SNR. Estimate sensitivity without processing gain.
rf-signal-chains.hint: Start with −174 dBm/Hz and add bandwidth, NF and required SNR.

rf-signal-chains.title: Find the unwanted input
rf-signal-chains.prompt: Desired RF is 125 MHz, LO is 110 MHz and a real mixer selects 15 MHz IF. Find the image.
rf-signal-chains.hint: Both signs of RF minus LO give the same real IF.

solution.text: The other side of the LO gives the same IF.

solution.answer: The image is at 95 MHz; filter it before the mixer.

rf-signal-chains.title: Two tones meet an intercept
rf-signal-chains.prompt: An amplifier has 15 dB gain and +5 dBm IIP3. Each input tone is −25 dBm. Estimate fundamental and IM3 output.
rf-signal-chains.hint: Use linear and cubic dB slopes separately.

solution.text: IM3 rises 3 dB per dB of input and meets the fundamental at IIP3.

transmission-lines.title: A slow clock with fast edges
transmission-lines.prompt: A 15 cm line has velocity 1.5 × 10⁸ m/s and carries a 2 MHz clock with 0.8 ns edges. Find flight time and the relevant timescale.
transmission-lines.hint: Compare flight time with edge time.

solution.text: Flight time (1 ns) exceeds the 0.8 ns edge.
The edge, not the 2 MHz clock period, decides. Treat the trace as a transmission line.

solution.answer: 1 ns flight; the 0.8 ns edge is the relevant timescale.

transmission-lines.title: A nonmatched load
transmission-lines.prompt: A 2 V source with 50 Ω resistance drives a 50 Ω line into 150 Ω. Find launch, reflection and first load voltage.
transmission-lines.hint: Use the source-to-line divider before the load arrives.

solution.text: The matched source absorbs the return, and DC agrees: 2 × 150/200 = 1.5 V.

transmission-lines.title: Locate a discontinuity
transmission-lines.prompt: A TDR sees a reflection 4 ns after launch on a line with velocity 1.6 × 10⁸ m/s. Find distance.

solution.text: 4 ns covers the distance twice.

differential-pairs.title: Translate a differential swing
differential-pairs.prompt: A pair has 1.2 V common mode and +0.6 V differential voltage. Find the two conductor voltages.
differential-pairs.hint: Split differential voltage equally around the common value.

differential-pairs.title: A timing mismatch becomes common mode
differential-pairs.prompt: Each conductor transitions by 0.5 V in 0.8 ns. One is delayed 80 ps. Estimate transient common-mode excursion for linear ramps.
differential-pairs.hint: Use half the single-ended transition times the fractional skew.

solution.text: While one line has moved and the other has not, the average shifts by half the partial movement.

differential-pairs.title: Allocate an electrical-length budget
differential-pairs.prompt: A channel allows 25 ps intrapair skew and propagation velocity is 160 mm/ns. Find the length difference budget and name other contributors.
differential-pairs.hint: Convert time to distance, then budget packages and connectors too.

solution.text: Package, connector, via and dielectric asymmetry share the same 25 ps.

solution.answer: 4 mm if all skew went to traces; less in practice.

sampling-converter-errors.title: Bins and ideal noise
sampling-converter-errors.prompt: A 14-bit converter has a 4 V span. Find bin width and ideal rms quantization noise.

solution.text: Error is spread evenly over ±q/2, with variance $q^2/12$.

sampling-converter-errors.title: A blocker survives software filtering
sampling-converter-errors.prompt: A 13 kHz input is sampled at 12 kS/s. Find its first-zone alias and explain whether a 2 kHz digital low-pass removes it.
sampling-converter-errors.hint: Find the distance to a multiple of the sample rate.

solution.text: After sampling, the 13 kHz tone is indistinguishable from 1 kHz.
1 kHz lies inside the 2 kHz passband, so the filter keeps it. Only an analog filter before the ADC can remove it.

solution.answer: Aliases to 1 kHz; the digital filter does not remove it.

sampling-converter-errors.title: Budget a source resistance
sampling-converter-errors.prompt: A 16-bit ADC uses 30 pF sampling capacitance and 300 ns acquisition. Find the maximum R in the ideal full-span first-order model.

solution.text: Settle a full-span step to half an LSB: $e^{-t/\tau}\le2^{-17}$.

solution.answer: About 849 Ω total, including switch resistance.

adc-successive-approximation.title: Trace five trial bits
adc-successive-approximation.prompt: For an ideal 5-bit SAR with 1 V reference and input 0.43 V, determine the trials and result under the floor-bin convention.
adc-successive-approximation.hint: Start at half scale and keep a bit only if its trial does not exceed input.

adc-successive-approximation.title: Conversion charge and droop
adc-successive-approximation.prompt: A SAR draws an 80 pC reference packet at 500 kS/s from 2.2 μF effective capacitance. Find average current and immediate ideal droop.
adc-successive-approximation.hint: Average demand and impulse response are different.

solution.answer: 40 µA average, 36 µV droop per conversion.

adc-successive-approximation.title: A serial link limits throughput
adc-successive-approximation.prompt: An ADC transaction uses 16 result bits plus 8 status bits. A 12 MHz serial clock supports no overlap and 0.5 μs overhead. Find maximum transaction rate.
adc-successive-approximation.hint: Include the bits and the gap.

adc-flash-pipeline.title: Comparator growth
adc-flash-pipeline.prompt: How many ideal full-flash comparators are required for 6 bits and 10 bits?
adc-flash-pipeline.hint: Every internal threshold needs a comparison.

solution.text: $N$ bits need a comparator for each of $2^N-1$ internal thresholds.

adc-flash-pipeline.title: A redundant stage stays reversible
adc-flash-pipeline.prompt: For normalized input x = −0.4, compute the ideal 1.5-bit decision and residue, then reconstruct x.
adc-flash-pipeline.hint: Use thresholds at ±0.25 and r = 2x − d.

adc-flash-pipeline.title: Rate is not immediate response
adc-flash-pipeline.prompt: A 125 MS/s ADC has eight sample-clock cycles of latency. Find latency and sample spacing.
adc-flash-pipeline.hint: Both quantities use the same clock but different cycle counts.

solution.text: A new sample appears every 8 ns, but each result arrives 64 ns after its sampling instant.

adc-integrating-delta-sigma.title: Cancel integrator values
adc-integrating-delta-sigma.prompt: An integrating ADC uses 80 ms input integration and a 2.5 V reference; rundown lasts 24 ms. Find the constant input voltage.

solution.text: The integrator returns to its start, so input charge equals reference charge.

adc-integrating-delta-sigma.title: Interpret a one-bit stream
adc-integrating-delta-sigma.prompt: A normalized ±1 feedback stream contains 700 positive decisions and 300 negative decisions. What input average does ideal bounded charge balance indicate?
adc-integrating-delta-sigma.hint: Average the actual feedback levels, not the unsigned bits alone.

solution.text: Each decision feeds back +1 or −1.

adc-integrating-delta-sigma.title: A sinc filter is not instantaneous
adc-integrating-delta-sigma.prompt: A sinc³ teaching decimator has modulator clock 128 kHz and M = 128. Find output rate and group delay.
adc-integrating-delta-sigma.hint: Use three boxcar delays at modulator rate.

solution.text: Each boxcar of length M has delay $(M-1)/2$ modulator clocks.

dac-architectures-output.title: Maximum code is below reference
dac-architectures-output.prompt: A 10-bit ideal DAC has 2.048 V reference and denominator 2ᴺ. Find the step, output at code 700 and output at maximum code.
dac-architectures-output.hint: There are 1024 code weights but maximum unsigned code is 1023.

dac-architectures-output.title: A major carry exposes mismatch
dac-architectures-output.prompt: An 8-bit weighted-current DAC has ideal lower-bit sum 127 units, but its MSB is 126.8 units. What happens from code 127 to 128?
dac-architectures-output.hint: Compare sums before and after the carry.

solution.text: All lower bits on: 127 units.
Only the MSB on: 126.8 units.

dac-architectures-output.title: Carrier, resolution and ripple
dac-architectures-output.prompt: A 100 MHz timer uses 10-bit PWM and 1 ms RC. At 3.3 V half duty, estimate carrier and ripple.
dac-architectures-output.hint: The period has 1024 counts; use the small-ripple RC expression.

solution.answer: 97.7 kHz carrier; about 8.4 mV p-p ripple.

digital-logic-timing.title: Check logic compatibility
digital-logic-timing.prompt: A driver guarantees 0.25 V low and 2.9 V high. The receiver allows low up to 0.7 V and requires high at least 2.2 V. Find margins.

solution.text: Valid only if the driver meets these levels at the actual load, temperature and supply.

digital-logic-timing.title: Find an allowed period
digital-logic-timing.prompt: Use tCQ,max = 1 ns, path = 6 ns, setup = 0.5 ns, uncertainty = 0.3 ns and positive capture skew = 0.2 ns. Find minimum period.
digital-logic-timing.hint: Later capture helps the next-edge setup check.

digital-logic-timing.title: A pulse crosses slowly
digital-logic-timing.prompt: A 5 ns source pulse goes into a two-flop synchronizer clocked every 20 ns. Is capture guaranteed?
digital-logic-timing.hint: Synchronization probability and pulse visibility are different questions.

solution.text: The pulse (5 ns) is shorter than the clock period (20 ns).
The pulse can begin and end between two receiving edges, so no flip-flop ever samples it high.
Stretch the pulse, convert it to a toggle, or use a request/acknowledge handshake.

solution.answer: No: the pulse can fall between clock edges.

em-fields.title: Derive a coax from its dimensions
em-fields.prompt: A coaxial cable has inner radius 0.5 mm, outer radius 1.75 mm and PTFE dielectric with εr = 2.1. Find C′, L′, Z₀ and the wave velocity.
em-fields.hint: Every result depends on ln(b/a); compute it once.

solution.text: Every coax formula depends on $\ln(b/a)$.

em-fields.title: Find the AC resistance of a thin wire
em-fields.prompt: At 100 MHz, find the skin depth in copper (ρ = 1.72×10⁻⁸ Ω·m) and the resistance per metre of a 0.5 mm diameter wire. Compare with its DC resistance.
em-fields.hint: δ falls as 1/√f from 66 µm at 1 MHz; the current flows in a layer of area 2πaδ.

solution.text: Current flows in a ring of circumference $2\pi a$ and thickness δ.

solution.answer: δ = 6.6 µm; $R'_{ac}$ ≈ 1.66 Ω/m, about 19× the DC value.

em-fields.title: Estimate inductive crosstalk
em-fields.prompt: A victim loop 3 cm long has its two conductors 5 mm and 7 mm from a long aggressor wire. The aggressor carries a 0.5 A step with a 2 ns rise. Estimate the mutual inductance and the induced voltage.
em-fields.hint: Integrate B = μ₀I/(2πr) across the loop.

solution.text: Integrate $B=\mu_0I/(2\pi r)$ from $r_1$ to $r_2$ over length ℓ.

solution.answer: $M$ ≈ 2.0 nH; about 0.5 V during the edge.

rf-components-smith.title: Find where a bypass capacitor stops working
rf-components-smith.prompt: A 10 nF capacitor has 0.8 nH of mounting inductance. Find its self-resonant frequency and its reactance at 200 MHz.

solution.answer: Resonates at 56 MHz; at 200 MHz it looks like +j0.93 Ω, essentially an inductor.

rf-components-smith.title: Convert an inductor's loss to parallel form
rf-components-smith.prompt: A 470 nH coil has 0.8 Ω effective series resistance at 25 MHz. Find Q, the parallel equivalent resistance, the capacitance that resonates it and the tank bandwidth.
rf-components-smith.hint: R_p = R_s(1 + Q²); bandwidth is f₀/Q.

solution.answer: Q = 92, $R_p$ ≈ 6.8 kΩ, C = 86 pF, B ≈ 271 kHz.

rf-components-smith.title: Design and stress a quarter-wave transformer
rf-components-smith.prompt: Match a 12.5 Ω load to 50 Ω at 1 GHz with a quarter-wave line on a board with effective permittivity 4. Find the line impedance and length, then the return loss at 1.2 GHz.
rf-components-smith.hint: Z_T = √(Z₀Z_L). At 1.2 GHz the same line is 108° long; use the general Z_in formula.

solution.answer: 25 Ω, 37.5 mm; at 1.2 GHz the return loss falls to 12.9 dB.

oscillators-pll.title: Size a Colpitts oscillator
oscillators-pll.prompt: Design a 5 MHz Colpitts oscillator with a 2.2 µH inductor of Q = 40 and equal capacitors. Find C₁, C₂ and the minimum transconductance.
oscillators-pll.hint: C_s = 1/(ω₀²L), then g_m > rω₀²C₁C₂ with r = ω₀L/Q.

solution.text: Two equal capacitors in series give $C/2$.

oscillators-pll.title: Predict crystal pulling from layout
oscillators-pll.prompt: A 25 MHz crystal has C_m = 8 fF and C₀ = 3 pF and is calibrated for a 10 pF load. The board actually presents 12 pF. Find the frequency error.
oscillators-pll.hint: f_L ≈ f_s[1 + C_m/(2(C₀ + C_L))]; compare the two loads.

solution.answer: The oscillator runs about 1.0 kHz (41 ppm) low; reduce the load capacitors by the stray.

oscillators-pll.title: Design a charge-pump loop filter
oscillators-pll.prompt: A 2.4 GHz synthesizer uses a 10 MHz reference, I_cp = 0.5 mA and K_v = 2π × 100 MHz/V. Choose R and C for f_n = 50 kHz and ζ = 0.7, and find how much reference phase noise is amplified in-band.
oscillators-pll.hint: N = f_out/f_ref; C = I_cpK_v/(2πNω_n²) and R = 2ζ/(ω_nC).

solution.answer: C ≈ 2.1 nF, R ≈ 2.1 kΩ; reference noise rises 47.6 dB in-band.

antennas-propagation.title: Judge a short antenna
antennas-propagation.prompt: A 15 cm centre-fed wire dipole with triangular current is used at 27 MHz. Find its feed-referred radiation resistance and efficiency if conductor and matching losses total 3 Ω. How much improvement could ideal matching alone provide if |Γ| = 0.5?
antennas-propagation.hint: Use effective length ℓ/2, then R_rad = 20π²(ℓ/λ)². Mismatch accepts a fraction 1 − |Γ|².

solution.text: Triangular current gives effective length ℓ/2.

solution.answer: $R_{rad}$ ≈ 0.036 Ω, efficiency ≈ 1.2%. Matching gains only 1.25 dB; loss is the real problem.

antennas-propagation.title: Budget a sub-GHz link
antennas-propagation.prompt: A 915 MHz link uses 14 dBm transmit power, 0 dBi antennas, −110 dBm receiver sensitivity and a 15 dB fade margin. Estimate free-space range.
antennas-propagation.hint: Find the path loss at 1 m, then the extra loss the budget allows.

solution.text: Free-space loss grows 20 dB per decade of distance.

antennas-propagation.title: Estimate current on an electrically short conductor
antennas-propagation.prompt: A screening target is 40 dBµV/m peak at 3 m. What peak common-mode current corresponds to that field on a 15 cm conductor at 100 MHz under E_cm ≈ 1.26×10⁻⁶ fℓI/r? State two model assumptions that a measurement must check.
antennas-propagation.hint: Convert 40 dBµV/m to 100 µV/m peak. Use SI units and check electrical length.

solution.text: The conductor is λ/20 (short, roughly uniform current) and 3 m is one wavelength, near the far-field boundary. Also check the ground-reflection geometry and detector type.

solution.answer: About 16 µA peak, which is a screening estimate, not a compliance result.

digital-signal-integrity.title: Find bandwidth and critical length from a rise time
digital-signal-integrity.prompt: A logic family has 0.5 ns edges on FR-4 (signal speed 15 cm/ns). Estimate the bandwidth the edge occupies and the trace length above which it should be treated as a transmission line.
digital-signal-integrity.hint: Use 0.35/t_r, then the t_r/6 delay rule.

solution.answer: About 700 MHz; traces longer than ≈ 1.25 cm need line treatment.

digital-signal-integrity.title: Choose a series resistor and compare parallel termination
digital-signal-integrity.prompt: A 15 Ω CMOS driver at 1.8 V drives a 60 Ω trace to one receiver. Choose a series termination, then find the static power if a 60 Ω parallel termination to ground were used instead.
digital-signal-integrity.hint: Series: R_out + R_ser = Z₀. Parallel: V²/R while high.

solution.answer: Use 47 Ω in series; parallel termination would cost 54 mW per line when high.

digital-signal-integrity.title: Estimate eye opening from channel bandwidth
digital-signal-integrity.prompt: A 500 Mbit/s link passes through a channel modelled as a single pole at 200 MHz. Estimate the worst-case eye height sampled at mid-bit and at the end of the bit.

solution.text: An isolated bit reaches $1-e^{-t_s/\tau}$; the opposite worst case leaves $e^{-t_s/\tau}$ behind. Eye height is the difference.

solution.answer: About 43% at mid-bit and 84% at the end of the bit.

uart-rs232.title: Decode a frame
uart-rs232.prompt: After the start bit, a receiver samples 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, then a high stop bit. What byte was sent?

solution.text: The first sample is bit 0 (the LSB).

uart-rs232.title: Check a baud divisor
uart-rs232.prompt: A 48 MHz peripheral clock with 16× oversampling must generate 230 400 baud. Find the integer divisor and the actual rate error.

solution.text: Use 13.

uart-rs232.title: Derive the tolerance for a parity frame
uart-rs232.prompt: For an 8E1 frame (eight data bits, even parity, one stop bit) with 16× oversampling, find the maximum total clock mismatch.
uart-rs232.hint: The stop bit is now the eleventh bit after the start edge (k = 10).

solution.text: Start (k = 0), eight data (1–8), parity (9), stop (10).

spi-interfaces.title: Identify an SPI mode
spi-interfaces.prompt: A peripheral's clock idles high and it samples data on falling edges. Which mode is it?
spi-interfaces.hint: From a high idle, the first edge is falling.

solution.text: Clock idles high: CPOL = 1.
From a high idle the first (leading) edge is falling; sampling there means CPHA = 0.

spi-interfaces.title: Find the maximum read clock
spi-interfaces.prompt: Flight time is 1.5 ns each way, the peripheral clock-to-output is 12 ns, the controller needs 4 ns setup and you want 2.5 ns margin. Find the maximum SCLK for opposite-edge capture.
spi-interfaces.hint: Half a period must cover the whole round trip.

spi-interfaces.title: Time a daisy chain update
spi-interfaces.prompt: Four 16-bit LED drivers are daisy-chained at 10 MHz. How long does one update take, and what is the maximum update rate ignoring CS overhead?
spi-interfaces.hint: All bits pass through every device.

solution.answer: 6.4 µs per update, about 156 k updates/s.

i2c-bus.title: Size standard-mode pull-ups
i2c-bus.prompt: A 5 V standard-mode bus has 300 pF of capacitance and devices sinking 3 mA at 0.4 V. Find the allowed pull-up range.

solution.text: Standard mode allows 1000 ns from 30% to 70%, which is $0.847RC$.
Anything between the limits: 2.2–3.3 kΩ.

i2c-bus.title: Derive the Fast-mode Plus clock
i2c-bus.prompt: Fast-mode Plus specifies t_LOW ≥ 0.5 µs, t_HIGH ≥ 0.26 µs and maximum edges of 120 ns. Find the maximum SCL frequency.
i2c-bus.hint: Add the four parts of one period.

solution.text: Low time, rising edge, high time, falling edge.

i2c-bus.title: Encode an address and count a read
i2c-bus.prompt: A display controller has 7-bit address 0x3C. Give the transmitted address bytes for write and read, and count the clocks to read two bytes from register 0x10.
i2c-bus.hint: Shift left one bit and append R/W. Each byte plus ACK is nine clocks.

solution.text: START, 0x78, register 0x10, repeated START, 0x79, data, data, STOP.

rs485-can.title: Count fractional-load nodes
rs485-can.prompt: How many quarter-unit-load RS-485 receivers present the same DC load as 32 standard unit loads?
rs485-can.hint: A quarter unit load is 48 kΩ.

rs485-can.title: Bias an idle bus
rs485-can.prompt: A 3.3 V bias network must hold an idle, doubly terminated RS-485 bus at 250 mV differential. Find the bias resistors.

solution.text: Two 120 Ω terminations in parallel give 60 Ω between the bias resistors.

rs485-can.title: Find a CAN bus length limit
rs485-can.prompt: At 250 kbit/s a controller uses sixteen 250 ns quanta with an 8 tq propagation segment. Transceivers add 200 ns each way and the cable delay is 5 ns/m. Find the maximum length.

usb-ethernet.title: Encode with stuffing
usb-ethernet.prompt: Encode seven consecutive 1 bits in USB NRZI starting from the J state.
usb-ethernet.hint: After six 1s insert a 0; a 0 toggles the line.

solution.text: A 1 holds the line; a 0 toggles.

solution.tex: J\ J\ J\ J\ J\ J\ K\ K

usb-ethernet.title: Change the termination
usb-ethernet.prompt: If each USB high-speed line were terminated with 50 Ω to ground at both ends instead of 45 Ω, what differential swing would the 17.78 mA driver produce?
usb-ethernet.hint: The driven line sees both terminations in parallel.

solution.text: 11% too large, and 100 Ω differential termination mismatches a 90 Ω cable.

usb-ethernet.title: Compute payload efficiency
usb-ethernet.prompt: Find the wire efficiency of Ethernet frames with a 512-byte payload, and the UDP payload rate on a 100 Mbit/s link.
usb-ethernet.hint: Overhead is 38 byte-times per frame; IPv4 + UDP headers take 28 bytes of payload.

solution.answer: 93.1% on the wire, about 88 Mbit/s of UDP data.

rf-amplifiers.title: Find the maximum unilateral gain
rf-amplifiers.prompt: A transistor has |S₂₁| = 4, |S₁₁| = 0.5 and |S₂₂| = 0.7, with S₁₂ negligible. Find its gain in a 50 Ω system and its maximum gain with conjugate matching.

solution.text: With $S_{12}\approx0$ and 50 Ω terminations, the transducer gain is $|S_{21}|^2$.
Input matching adds $-10\log0.75$ = 1.25 dB and output matching adds $-10\log0.51$ = 2.9 dB.

solution.answer: 12.0 dB in 50 Ω; 16.2 dB conjugately matched.

rf-amplifiers.title: Design a degenerated LNA input
rf-amplifiers.prompt: A 5.8 GHz LNA transistor has C_gs = 0.3 pF and g_m = 30 mS. Find L_s for a 50 Ω input and L_g for resonance.
rf-amplifiers.hint: L_s = 50/ω_T with ω_T = g_m/C_gs; L_g + L_s = 1/(ω₀²C_gs).

solution.text: The degenerated input looks like $\omega_TL_s$ of real resistance.

solution.answer: $L_s$ = 0.50 nH, $L_g$ = 2.0 nH (include pad and via inductance).

rf-amplifiers.title: Size a power amplifier load
rf-amplifiers.prompt: A class A PA runs from 5 V with a 0.5 V knee and must deliver 2 W. Find the optimum load and the Q of the L network that presents it from 50 Ω.

solution.text: Class A peaks at 50% efficiency.

solution.answer: $R_{opt}$ ≈ 5.1 Ω, Q ≈ 3.0; supply at least 4 W.

rf-filters.title: Find the order for a stopband
rf-filters.prompt: A low-pass filter must attenuate 60 dB at three times its cutoff. Find the Butterworth order and the order for a 0.5 dB Chebyshev (ε² = 0.122).
rf-filters.hint: Use the two order formulas with A = 60 dB.

rf-filters.title: Scale a prototype
rf-filters.prompt: Design a third-order Butterworth low-pass for 30 MHz between 50 Ω terminations.

solution.text: Third-order Butterworth: $g_1=1,\ g_2=2,\ g_3=1$ (shunt C, series L, shunt C).

rf-filters.title: Estimate a narrow filter's loss
rf-filters.prompt: A fifth-order Butterworth band-pass (g = 0.618, 1.618, 2, 1.618, 0.618) has 2% fractional bandwidth. Find its insertion loss with Q_u = 150 inductors and with Q_u = 2000 acoustic resonators.

solution.answer: 9.4 dB with lumped inductors, 0.7 dB with acoustic resonators.

modulation.title: Find AM sideband power
modulation.prompt: A 10 W carrier is amplitude modulated with m = 0.5 by a single tone. Find the sideband power and its fraction of the total.
modulation.hint: Each sideband carries m²/4 of the carrier power.

solution.answer: 1.25 W in the sidebands, 11% of the total.

modulation.title: Apply Carson's rule
modulation.prompt: A narrowband FM radio uses 5 kHz peak deviation and audio up to 3 kHz. Find the modulation index and occupied bandwidth.

modulation.title: Compare a link with the Shannon limit
modulation.prompt: A 20 MHz channel uses 64-QAM with roll-off 0.35 and has 25 dB SNR. Find the symbol rate, bit rate and Shannon capacity.
modulation.hint: R_s = B/(1 + α); R_b = 6R_s; C = B log₂(1 + SNR).

solution.text: 64-QAM carries 6 bits per symbol.

line-supplies.title: Find ripple from the reservoir
line-supplies.prompt: A 50 Hz bridge rectifier charges 3300 µF and supplies 2 A. Estimate the peak-to-peak ripple.

solution.text: A 50 Hz bridge recharges every 10 ms.

solution.answer: About 6 V p-p, which is too much for most designs.

line-supplies.title: Estimate conduction time and pulse current
line-supplies.prompt: A 60 Hz full-wave supply has a 20 V peak and 2 V ripple at 1 A. Find the conduction time and the average diode current during conduction.
line-supplies.hint: cos θ_c = 1 − ΔV/V_p; the half-cycle charge I/(2f) is delivered in t_c.

solution.text: Each half-cycle the diodes replace $I/2f$ = 8.33 mC.

solution.answer: About 1.2 ms, 6.9 A average (peak about twice that).

line-supplies.title: Rate a transformer
line-supplies.prompt: A bridge rectifier from a 12 V rms secondary must supply 1.5 A DC. If the secondary rms current is about 1.8 times the DC current, what VA rating is needed?

solution.text: Choose the next size up, 40 VA.

regulator-ics.title: Set a 317 output
regulator-ics.prompt: Design a 317 for 12 V with R₁ = 240 Ω, then compute the actual output with a standard 2.05 kΩ for R₂ and I_ADJ = 50 µA.

solution.answer: Ideal 2064 Ω; with 2.05 kΩ the output is 12.03 V.

regulator-ics.title: Size the adjust capacitor
regulator-ics.prompt: With R₂ = 2 kΩ, what C_ADJ puts the bypass corner at or below 10 Hz?

solution.text: 10 µF, with a diode from ADJ to OUT to discharge it safely.

regulator-ics.title: Make an LED current source
regulator-ics.prompt: Use a 317 to drive LEDs at 350 mA from 12 V with 2 V dropout. Find R, its power and the maximum LED string voltage.

solution.answer: 3.6 Ω, 0.44 W; LED string up to 8.75 V.

thermal-soa.title: Choose a heat sink
thermal-soa.prompt: A device dissipates 25 W with θ_JC = 1.5 °C/W and θ_CS = 0.3 °C/W. Ambient is 40 °C and the junction must stay below 125 °C. Find the maximum θ_SA.

thermal-soa.title: Find a pulse temperature rise
thermal-soa.prompt: A data sheet gives Z_th = 0.6 °C/W for 5 ms pulses. How hot does the junction get above the case during an 80 W, 5 ms pulse?

thermal-soa.title: Derate a power rating
thermal-soa.prompt: A transistor is rated 150 W at 25 °C case with T_J,max = 175 °C. What can it dissipate with its case at 110 °C?

isolated-offline.title: Size a bulk capacitor
isolated-offline.prompt: A 100 W-input supply must hold up for 16.7 ms while its bulk falls from 150 V to 100 V. Find the minimum capacitance.

solution.text: The capacitor's energy drop must supply $P\,t_h$.

isolated-offline.title: Check flyback drain stress
isolated-offline.prompt: A flyback from a 375 V maximum bulk produces 5 V with a 0.5 V diode and N_p/N_s = 18. Find the reflected voltage and the drain voltage before the leakage spike.

solution.answer: $V_R$ = 99 V; drain at 474 V before the spike.

isolated-offline.title: Compute power factor
isolated-offline.prompt: A rectifier draws 0.8 A rms with a 0.5 A rms fundamental in phase with the voltage. Find the power factor.

solution.text: The fundamental is in phase: cos φ₁ = 1.

batteries-protection.title: Estimate battery run time
batteries-protection.prompt: A 3000 mAh, 3.6 V cell powers a load averaging 150 mA. Estimate the run time and stored energy.

solution.text: High current bursts and cold reduce usable capacity.

batteries-protection.title: Find usable capacitor energy
batteries-protection.prompt: A 5 F capacitor charged to 5 V feeds a converter that works down to 2.5 V. Find the usable energy and its fraction of the stored energy.

batteries-protection.title: Set a hot-swap ramp
batteries-protection.prompt: A hot-swap controller limits inrush into 470 µF on a 48 V bus to 2 A. Find the ramp time and the energy the MOSFET absorbs.

solution.text: With constant current charging, the pass device absorbs as much as the capacitor stores.

noise-fundamentals.title: Add uncorrelated noise
noise-fundamentals.prompt: Three independent sources contribute 3, 4 and 12 nV/√Hz at an amplifier input. Find the total.

solution.text: Removing the 3 and 4 nV sources would leave 12, only 8% less.

noise-fundamentals.title: Find resistor noise in a band
noise-fundamentals.prompt: Find the rms Johnson noise of a 100 kΩ resistor at room temperature over a 10 kHz bandwidth.
noise-fundamentals.hint: e_n = √(4kTR); multiply by √B for white noise.

noise-fundamentals.title: Convert noise figure to temperature
noise-fundamentals.prompt: An amplifier has a 2 dB noise figure. Find its noise temperature.

transistor-noise.title: Compute e_n and i_n
transistor-noise.prompt: Find the voltage and current noise of a BJT at 100 µA with r_bb′ = 50 Ω and β = 200.

solution.step: Collector shot noise referred to the input

transistor-noise.title: Choose a collector current
transistor-noise.prompt: A 2 kΩ source drives a BJT with β = 300. Find the optimum collector current and minimum noise figure, neglecting r_bb′.

solution.text: Balance $e_n$ and $i_nR_s$.

transistor-noise.title: Match a low source
transistor-noise.prompt: A 50 Ω source drives an amplifier whose noise resistance is 5 kΩ. What transformer turns ratio matches them?

solution.text: A transformer multiplies impedance by $n^2$.
The source appears as 5 kΩ; its signal and noise voltages both rise tenfold, so the amplifier's own noise matters less.

opamp-noise.title: Find feedback-network noise
opamp-noise.prompt: A noninverting amplifier has R_f = 99 kΩ and R_g = 1 kΩ. What Johnson noise do the feedback resistors contribute at the input?

opamp-noise.title: Judge an op amp on a high-impedance source
opamp-noise.prompt: A JFET op amp with 10 nV/√Hz and 2 fA/√Hz reads a 1 MΩ source. Does the op amp matter?

solution.answer: The op amp adds only 0.3%; the source dominates.

opamp-noise.title: Estimate e_nC noise
opamp-noise.prompt: A TIA op amp has 4 nV/√Hz, with 30 pF at its input and 1.5 pF of feedback capacitance. What is the output noise density from e_n above the feedback pole?

solution.text: Above the feedback pole the input and feedback capacitors form a capacitive divider.

solution.answer: About 84 nV/√Hz until the op amp's bandwidth limits it.

noise-measurement.title: Convert an rms reading
noise-measurement.prompt: A noise measurement reads 0.5 mV rms after a gain of 1000 and a single-pole 10 kHz filter. Find the input noise density.

noise-measurement.title: Compute noise figure from a Y-factor
noise-measurement.prompt: A noise source with 5 dB ENR produces a 3 dB increase in output noise when switched on. Find the noise figure.

noise-measurement.title: Find a lock-in's output noise
noise-measurement.prompt: A lock-in with a 0.3 s single-pole time constant sees 50 nV/√Hz of white noise around its reference. Find the output rms noise.

solution.step: Noise bandwidth of the output filter

solution.answer: About 46 nV rms, settling in about 1.5 s.
